# ChatonLM

> ChatonLM is a free, open-source desktop app for Windows 11 and Linux that brings the tools of local AI together in one window: chat, a model catalog, dictation, voice, proofreading, study and image generation. Models run on the user's own computer, with no account, no subscription and no telemetry.

Tools:

- {{h:tools.chat.name}}: {{h:tools.chat.text}}
- {{h:tools.hub.name}}: {{h:tools.hub.text}}
- {{h:tools.dictation.name}}: {{h:tools.dictation.text}}
- {{h:tools.voice.name}}: {{h:tools.voice.text}}
- {{h:tools.proofread.name}}: {{h:tools.proofread.text}}
- {{h:tools.study.name}}: {{h:tools.study.text}}
- {{h:tools.images.name}}: {{h:tools.images.text}}
- VS Code extension: the ChatonLM extension for VS Code (and VSCodium, from Open VSX) explains, fixes and completes code, writes tests and commit messages, gives spoken tours of a file or of changes, and offers hands-free voice and dictation, all with the models of the ChatonLM app on the same computer.

Facts:

- Price: free for life. Open-source software under the MIT license. No paid version, no subscription, no one-time purchase, no ads.
- Platforms: Windows 11 (installer) and Linux (AppImage and .deb), on 64-bit x86 PCs. No macOS version for now.
- Hardware: a graphics card makes models faster but is not required. For image generation it is strongly recommended: on the processor, an image takes several minutes.
- Interface languages: English, French and Spanish.
- Engine: ChatonLM includes its own engine, built on llama.cpp (MIT): models run on the graphics card through Vulkan, or on the processor, with optional NVIDIA acceleration (a CUDA 13 pack downloaded on demand, for GeForce RTX 20 series cards and newer with driver 580 or later; NVIDIA's license is shown first). Models come from Hugging Face (GGUF files). ChatonLM does not need Ollama and does not connect to an Ollama server; models already downloaded with Ollama can be imported in one click (they are copied, and Ollama is left untouched). ChatonLM is an independent project, not affiliated with Ollama.
- Image generation: in the chat, with the Image button or by asking a model that can use tools. Images are made on the user's computer by a built-in engine (stable-diffusion.cpp), with open image models chosen in ModelHub from Hugging Face (such as FLUX.2 klein and Z-Image), whose license (free use, non-commercial use, or a license to read) is shown for each one.
- Privacy: conversations, attachments, generated images, voice and settings stay on the user's computer. The app goes online only to browse and download models (image models included) and voices, to check for signed updates and newer versions of installed models and, if enabled, for web search (through ChatonLM's own search service, with no account; results from Brave Search, of which only titles and links are kept), remote models (off by default; with the user's own API key, from Ollama Cloud, OpenRouter, Mistral or any server compatible with the OpenAI API, so messages sent to one leave the computer; dictation never goes to one) and Easy Link (messages to the user's own Telegram or Discord bot, which go through that service, generated images included). Ephemeral chats, opened with the ghost kitten, stay out of the history and are erased, down to the database files, when the user opens another chat or quits, unless kept.
- Details: before an answer is read aloud, its text is prepared for the voice in each language (numbers, dates, times, units, currencies and version numbers written out, acronyms spelled out), in under a tenth of a millisecond per paragraph. A gauge shows how full the model's context is; past 80% the oldest messages are summarized automatically, or on demand, and the whole history stays visible. A model that loops is stopped or flagged. A graphics memory (VRAM) gauge shows each loaded model's share, and a snail flags a model running partly on the processor. Dictation is pasted where the cursor is. Proofreading and study can be set to "Auto": the largest model already loaded, or else the chat model. Loaded models are unloaded when the app quits (can be turned off). A global shortcut (off by default, Ctrl+Alt+R suggested) reads aloud the text selected in any app. Proofreading options keep the words in their order, the formatting, or numbers as digits. Text put on the clipboard by dictation and proofreading stays out of the clipboard history (and of Windows' cloud clipboard). The database is backed up before each format update and can be restored after going back to an older version. "Report a bug" (Settings › General) sends a message, with a diagnostic the user can read first, to chatonlm.com.
- VS Code extension: needs ChatonLM 0.9.4 or later on the same computer and VS Code 1.105 or later. It talks to the app through a local link (no network), only for editors paired with a code, and has no telemetry. Autocomplete, Easy Link notifications, the MCP server for the editor's agents and ChatonLM's models in VS Code's built-in chat are each off by default. Visual Studio Marketplace: https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=chatonlm.chatonlm ; Open VSX: https://open-vsx.org/extension/chatonlm/chatonlm
- Designed in France.
